public_rationale: This is a conditional forecast with no deadline. It applies only if OpenAI falls, read here as a WeWork-style collapse or valuation crash. The evidence does not show that this has happened. On 2026-02-27, OpenAI announced $110B in new investment at a $730B pre-money valuation, including $30B from SoftBank, $30B from NVIDIA and $50B from Amazon (e2). On 2026-03-31, Engadget reported that the round closed at $122B, with a post-money valuation of $852B (e1). The evidence contains nothing about OpenAI's valuation or condition between April and October 2026. Because the condition has not been shown to be met, the prediction cannot be scored yet. It remains open.
limitations: 'Falls' is not defined in the source. This assessment reads it as a collapse or steep valuation crash.
The evidence has no reports on OpenAI's valuation or financial condition after March 2026.
The funding details show who invested, but they say nothing about losses, because no collapse has been documented.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: If OpenAI falls, many parties besides SoftBank will struggle with the fallout.

statement.excerpt: If OpenAI falls, SoftBank will hardly be alone in struggling to pick the pieces.

our_interpretation: Antecedent: OpenAI 'falls', read as a collapse, near-bankruptcy or steep valuation crash like WeWork's, the comparison he draws.
Outcome: investors or partners other than SoftBank also suffer substantial losses or distress.
criteria.support_condition: OpenAI collapses or crashes in value, and parties besides SoftBank report substantial losses or distress from it.
criteria.contradiction_condition: OpenAI collapses or crashes in value, and SoftBank alone bears substantial losses.
